# Why this fixture is not `range-nested.qmd`

Both fixtures carry the nested shape and a plain range beside it. This one
also carries two shapes that fixture must not: a span that looks like a range
mark and is not one, and a range mark that indexes nothing. Each draws a
different answer out of the guard that hands a mark its position, and the
second of them draws a report — which is why they cannot live in a fixture
whose criterion is that it reports nothing at all.

A span carrying `range=` but no index class [quokka]{range="open"} is no mark,
so the guard gives it no position and neither traversal counts it.

A range mark that indexes nothing []{.index range="open"} takes a position all
the same, and plans no verdict at it. It is the shape where the two traversals
stop at different points: the collecting one derives no entry and plans
nothing, the emitting one reports why the mark indexes nothing. Both have
already taken the position by then.

# A range mark whose own content carries another mark

The emitting pass rewrites the inner mark before it reaches the outer one, so
the outer mark's visible text is not the same object in the two passes that
read it.

The discussion of [nixie [ogopogo]{.index}]{.index range="open"} begins here.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# A plain range of another term, opening inside the nested one

It opens and closes inside the nested range above, so the two overlap and a
verdict handed to the wrong mark shows as a span of the wrong width rather
than as a missing entry.

The discussion of [pooka]{.index range="open"} begins here.

{{< pagebreak >}}

And the discussion of [pooka]{.index range="close"} ends here.

{{< pagebreak >}}

And the discussion of [nixie [ogopogo]{.index}]{.index range="close"} ends
here.
